signs: Sudden death | high fever 104-107°F | salivation | neck/throat swelling | dyspnea | blood-tinged nasal discharge
diagnosis: History | clinical signs | blood smear | culture
treatment_raw: Penicillin + streptomycin; sulfadiazine IV; supportive fluids and antipyretic
prevention: HS vaccination (notes state March & September)
red_flags: Sudden death | severe dyspnea | rapidly progressive neck swelling
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Sudden lameness | hot painful muscle swelling | crepitation | gas | depression | death in 12-24 h
diagnosis: Clinical signs | swollen muscle | gas | smear
treatment_raw: High-dose penicillin + antitoxin; surgical debridement; prognosis may be poor
prevention: BQ vaccination
red_flags: Rapid swelling with gas | systemic collapse
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Fever | salivation | vesicles in mouth/tongue/feet | lameness | drop in milk | smacking lips
treatment_raw: No specific antiviral; symptomatic care; antiseptic mouth care; soft feed; foot care; antibiotics only for secondary bacterial infection
prevention: FMD vaccination every 6 months (per notes)
red_flags: Vesicular disease | herd outbreak | severe lameness
clinical_review_notes: Regulatory/reportable-disease handling and local veterinary authority guidance must be added before deployment.

cause: Staphylococcus aureus; Streptococcus spp.; Escherichia coli
signs: Hot painful swollen udder | abnormal milk with clots/watery/blood | fever
diagnosis: California Mastitis Test (CMT) | milk culture | somatic cell count (SCC)
treatment_raw: Intramammary antibiotics + systemic antibiotics when indicated + anti-inflammatory therapy + frequent milking
prevention: Milking hygiene | teat dip | dry-cow therapy
red_flags: Toxic mastitis | severe dehydration | recumbency
clinical_review_notes: Antibiotic choice, dose, route and milk-withdrawal period require veterinarian/culture-based validation.

signs: Late-term abortion | retained placenta | metritis | orchitis in bulls
treatment_raw: No effective routine treatment in herd-control context; culling/control measures recommended in notes
prevention: Vaccination of heifers 4-8 months (per notes)
red_flags: Abortion storm | zoonotic exposure risk
clinical_review_notes: Zoonotic/reportable disease. Treatment/control policies vary by country and must be replaced with official local guidance.

signs: High fever | anemia | pale/yellow mucous membranes | coffee-colored urine | tick infestation
treatment_raw: Imidocarb dipropionate 3 mg/kg IM; antipyretic; blood transfusion if severe; source notes also mention buparvaquone
prevention: Tick control | prophylactic treatment where appropriate
red_flags: Hemoglobinuria | severe anemia | collapse
clinical_review_notes: Source note mixes babesiosis therapy with buparvaquone, which is primarily used for theileriosis; veterinarian must correct before training as ground truth.

signs: Fever | enlarged lymph nodes | anemia | dyspnea | corneal opacity | drop in milk
treatment_raw: Buparvaquone 2.5 mg/kg IM + oxytetracycline + supportive care
prevention: Tick control
red_flags: Severe anemia | respiratory distress | recumbency
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Progressive anemia | pale mucous membranes | jaundice | weight loss | source notes state no fever
treatment_raw: Oxytetracycline 10 mg/kg for 5 days + imidocarb (per source notes)
prevention: Tick control
red_flags: Severe anemia | jaundice | collapse
clinical_review_notes: Clinical presentation and treatment regimen need veterinary validation; fever can occur in acute anaplasmosis.

signs: Diarrhea | weight loss | pot belly in calves | rough hair coat | anemia
treatment_raw: Albendazole 10 mg/kg OR fenbendazole 10 mg/kg OR ivermectin 0.2 mg/kg SC (per notes)
prevention: Strategic deworming; source notes say every 3 months
red_flags: Severe anemia | dehydration | failure to thrive
clinical_review_notes: Anthelmintic choice and schedule should be parasite-, region- and resistance-guided; validate dose and withdrawal times.

signs: Bottle jaw | anemia | weight loss | ascites | decreased production
treatment_raw: Triclabendazole 12 mg/kg OR closantel 10 mg/kg (per notes)
prevention: Snail control | avoid high-risk marshy grazing
red_flags: Severe anemia | ascites
clinical_review_notes: Drug dose, resistance patterns and meat/milk withdrawal periods require local veterinary validation.

signs: Downer cow | S-shaped neck | cold extremities | bloat | muscle tremors | unconsciousness
diagnosis: Periparturient history | clinical signs | low blood calcium; source notes use <5 mg/dL
treatment_raw: 20% calcium borogluconate 400-500 mL IV slowly; repeat after 6-8 h if needed (per notes)
prevention: Pre-calving dietary cation-anion management/anionic salts | vitamin D only under veterinary/nutrition guidance
red_flags: Recumbency after calving | bloat | unconsciousness | arrhythmia risk during IV calcium
clinical_review_notes: IV calcium can cause fatal arrhythmia if given improperly; administration must be veterinarian-supervised.

signs: Drop in milk | acetone odor on breath/urine | nervous signs | licking | weight loss
diagnosis: Ketone testing in urine/milk | blood glucose
treatment_raw: 50% dextrose 500 mL IV + propylene glycol 250 mL orally twice daily for 5 days + glucocorticoid (per notes)
prevention: Good transition diet | avoid over-conditioning
red_flags: Neurologic signs | severe anorexia | concurrent displaced abomasum
clinical_review_notes: Dose/regimen and differential diagnosis should be veterinarian-validated before clinical use.

signs: Distended left flank | respiratory distress | discomfort | kicking at belly
treatment_raw: Stomach tube for free gas; poloxalene 25-50 g orally; antifoaming agent; trocarization in life-threatening cases
prevention: Avoid sudden access to lush legumes | feed hay before high-risk pasture
red_flags: Severe respiratory distress | collapse | rapidly increasing left flank distension
clinical_review_notes: Trocarization is an invasive emergency procedure for trained veterinary personnel.

signs: Diarrhea | dehydration | depression | laminitis | rumen stasis
treatment_raw: Rumen lavage + IV sodium bicarbonate + fluids + thiamine + antibiotics (per notes)
prevention: Gradual grain introduction
red_flags: Severe dehydration | recumbency | shock | laminitis
clinical_review_notes: Treatment depends on severity and acid-base status; veterinarian must validate bicarbonate/antibiotic use.

cause: Escherichia coli; rotavirus; coccidia (examples in notes)
signs: Watery diarrhea | dehydration | depression | sunken eyes | cold extremities
treatment_raw: Oral electrolytes; IV fluids if severe; antibiotics only when bacterial sepsis/systemic infection is suspected; source notes specify E. coli
prevention: Cleanliness | adequate early colostrum; source notes specify within 2 hours
red_flags: Severe dehydration | inability to suck | cold extremities | blood in stool | sepsis
clinical_review_notes: Etiology-specific treatment is essential; routine antibiotics/antidiarrheals should not be encoded as universal ground truth.

signs: Fever | skin nodules 1-5 cm | nasal discharge | swollen lymph nodes | drop in milk
treatment_raw: Supportive/symptomatic care; antibiotics only for secondary bacterial infection; anti-inflammatory therapy; vector/fly control
prevention: LSD vaccination where officially recommended
red_flags: Widespread nodules | severe edema | herd outbreak
clinical_review_notes: May be reportable depending on jurisdiction; official control guidance should supersede generic notes.

signs: Severe lameness | swelling between claws | foul smell | reluctance to walk
treatment_raw: Clean/dry environment; systemic antibiotic and anti-inflammatory therapy when indicated; source notes mention CuSO4 foot bath + penicillin
prevention: Foot hygiene | dry environment | preventive foot-bath program where appropriate
red_flags: Severe lameness | deep tissue involvement | fever
clinical_review_notes: Copper sulfate concentration and antimicrobial regimen require veterinary validation.

signs: Fetal membranes retained >12-24 h | foul odor | fever | anorexia
treatment_raw: Do not forcibly pull; systemic antibiotics if systemic illness/metritis; source notes mention PGF2α, uterine pessaries and fluids if toxic
prevention: Good transition nutrition | selenium/vitamin E when deficient | clean calving environment
red_flags: Toxic metritis | fever | anorexia | dehydration
clinical_review_notes: Routine uterine pessaries/PGF2α are not universally recommended; veterinarian should define evidence-based protocol.

signs: Prolonged labor | fetus not delivered | persistent straining | ruptured water bag without progress
treatment_raw: Correct fetal position and controlled obstetrical traction when appropriate; cesarean section if indicated; post-calving supportive therapy as required
prevention: Appropriate sire selection | heifer/cow nutrition and calving management
red_flags: No progress in labor | malpresentation | exhausted dam | fetal distress
clinical_review_notes: Obstetrical traction and C-section require trained veterinary personnel; avoid fixed time thresholds as sole trigger.

signs: Large red uterine mass protruding from vulva after calving
treatment_raw: Protect/clean prolapsed uterus; epidural; careful replacement; retention technique if indicated; supportive antibiotics/oxytocin as clinically indicated
prevention: Reduce dystocia and metabolic risk; periparturient management
red_flags: Hemorrhage | shock | contaminated/traumatized uterus
clinical_review_notes: Source note specifies KMnO4; antiseptic choice/concentration should not be used without veterinary protocol.

cause: Postpartum uterine infection with persistent corpus luteum
signs: Anestrus | purulent vaginal discharge | enlarged uterus
treatment_raw: PGF2α when a functional corpus luteum is present; source notes say 2 doses 11 days apart and intrauterine antibiotics
prevention: Clean calving | early diagnosis/treatment of metritis
red_flags: Systemic illness | fever | toxic metritis differential
clinical_review_notes: Regimen must depend on reproductive status and veterinarian examination; intrauterine antibiotics are not universally indicated.

cause: Mannheimia spp.; Pasteurella spp.; respiratory viruses
signs: Fever | cough | nasal discharge | dyspnea | decreased appetite
diagnosis: Clinical examination | lung auscultation | imaging where available
treatment_raw: Veterinary-selected antimicrobial when bacterial disease is suspected + NSAID/supportive care; source notes mention bronchodilator/nebulization
prevention: Ventilation | colostrum | vaccination as appropriate
red_flags: Open-mouth breathing | cyanosis | severe respiratory distress
clinical_review_notes: Antimicrobial selection and duration should follow local stewardship and diagnosis.

signs: Red nose | fever | nasal discharge | conjunctivitis | abortion | drop in milk
treatment_raw: Supportive care; antibiotics only for secondary bacterial infection
prevention: IBR vaccination according to local herd program
red_flags: Abortion outbreak | severe respiratory disease
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Intense itching | hair loss | thickened skin | crusts
treatment_raw: Ivermectin 0.2 mg/kg SC with repeat after 14 days + amitraz dip (per notes)
prevention: Isolation | environmental hygiene/disinfection
red_flags: Severe skin lesions | marked weight loss
clinical_review_notes: Agent-specific diagnosis, dose, retreatment interval and food-animal withdrawal requirements need validation.

signs: Circular hairless scaly patches on head/neck
diagnosis: Clinical exam | fungal microscopy/culture; source notes mention Wood's lamp
treatment_raw: Topical antifungal/environmental management; source notes mention oral griseofulvin and lime sulfur
prevention: Hygiene | reduce crowding | disinfection
red_flags: Extensive lesions | immunocompromised animal
clinical_review_notes: Griseofulvin use in food animals may be restricted/prohibited; do not use source note as prescribing ground truth.

signs: Behavior change | aggression or depression | excessive salivation | paralysis | difficulty swallowing
diagnosis: Exposure history | clinical suspicion | laboratory confirmation, generally postmortem
treatment_raw: No treatment for clinically affected animal; isolate and notify veterinary/public-health authorities
prevention: Rabies vaccination according to local risk and regulations
red_flags: Neurologic signs + salivation | human exposure risk
clinical_review_notes: Fatal zoonosis. App must direct users to emergency veterinary/public-health authorities and avoid handling suspected animals.

signs: Stiff gait | saw-horse stance | lockjaw | prolapsed third eyelid | convulsions
treatment_raw: Antitoxin + antimicrobial therapy + muscle relaxation/sedation + quiet low-stimulus environment + wound management
prevention: Vaccination | appropriate wound prophylaxis
red_flags: Dysphagia | respiratory compromise | recumbency/convulsions
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Sudden death | absent/incomplete rigor mortis | dark blood from orifices | swollen carcass
diagnosis: Do not open carcass; official veterinary laboratory diagnosis
treatment_raw: Urgent official veterinary control; antimicrobial treatment may be considered only under authority/veterinarian direction in live suspected cases
prevention: Vaccination in endemic areas | official carcass disposal/control
red_flags: Sudden unexplained death | bleeding from orifices | human exposure risk
clinical_review_notes: High-risk zoonotic/reportable disease. Source instruction to use blood smear/penicillin must not replace official anthrax protocol; carcass must not be opened.

signs: Night blindness | rough hair coat | poor growth | reproductive problems
diagnosis: Diet history | clinical assessment | laboratory testing when available
treatment_raw: Vitamin A supplementation/injection based on veterinarian/nutritionist assessment; source notes state 2-5 million IU IM
prevention: Adequate green forage or formulated vitamin A supplementation
red_flags: Neurologic/visual impairment in young animals
clinical_review_notes: High-dose vitamin A can be harmful; dose should not be treated as universal.

signs: Stiff gait | difficulty standing | sudden death in calves
diagnosis: Clinical assessment | selenium/vitamin E status | muscle enzymes where available
treatment_raw: Selenium + vitamin E therapy under veterinarian supervision
prevention: Balanced mineral program based on local deficiency risk
red_flags: Sudden death | severe weakness | respiratory involvement
clinical_review_notes: Selenium has a narrow safety margin; exact dose must be veterinarian-prescribed.

cause: Copper deficiency or impaired copper availability
signs: Rough coat | faded coat color | anemia | diarrhea | periocular depigmentation
treatment_raw: Copper supplementation based on confirmed deficiency
prevention: Balanced mineral supplementation
red_flags: Severe anemia | chronic wasting
clinical_review_notes: Copper toxicity risk varies by species and formulation; do not encode generic injection/oral dosing without validation.

signs: Pica | bone/soil licking | poor growth | depraved appetite
diagnosis: Dietary assessment | serum phosphorus with clinical context
treatment_raw: Dietary phosphorus supplementation such as dicalcium phosphate when indicated
prevention: Balanced mineral supplementation
red_flags: Severe pica | poor growth | fractures
clinical_review_notes: Source note links phosphorus deficiency directly to milk fever; this is misleading and should be corrected before model training.

signs: Panting | drooling | respiratory rate >80/min (per notes) | drop in milk/feed intake
treatment_raw: Immediate cooling: shade, airflow/fans, sprinklers/water cooling, drinking water, electrolyte/fluid support as indicated
prevention: Shade | ventilation/cooling | adequate water
red_flags: Open-mouth breathing | collapse | very high body temperature
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Prolonged recumbency secondary to metabolic, traumatic, neurologic or other disease
signs: Unable to stand for >24 h (source definition)
diagnosis: Identify primary cause | physical/neurologic exam | blood tests as indicated
treatment_raw: Treat underlying cause + frequent repositioning + deep bedding/supportive nursing; flotation/lifting only with trained personnel
prevention: Prevent metabolic disease | safe flooring | early treatment of recumbent cows
red_flags: Prolonged recumbency | pressure injury | severe pain | inability to eat/drink
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Urinary stone formation; common in males
signs: Straining | dribbling urine | swollen prepuce | tail swishing
treatment_raw: Emergency relief of obstruction; surgical options include tube cystostomy or urethrostomy; urinary acidification such as ammonium chloride when appropriate
prevention: Balanced ration; source notes use Ca:P ratio 2:1 | adequate water | urinary acidification when indicated
red_flags: No urine | abdominal distension | uroperitoneum | severe pain
clinical_review_notes: Obstructed male is an emergency. Surgical procedure and ammonium chloride dose require veterinarian management.

signs: Swollen/infected navel | fever | swollen joints | lameness | depression
diagnosis: Clinical examination | neonatal history | culture/bloodwork when available
treatment_raw: Prompt veterinarian-selected systemic antibiotics + NSAID/supportive care; navel care
prevention: Clean calving | prompt appropriate navel disinfection | colostrum
red_flags: Septicemia | multiple swollen joints | recumbency
clinical_review_notes: Antibiotic choice/duration should be culture and stewardship guided; iodine concentration for navel dipping must be protocol-defined.

cause: Abomasal displacement, usually around early lactation
signs: Sudden drop in milk | anorexia/reduced appetite | characteristic ping on left or right side
diagnosis: Auscultation/percussion | clinical examination | ultrasonography where available
treatment_raw: Surgical correction is common; rolling may be used selectively but has recurrence/risk considerations
prevention: Transition-cow nutrition and management
red_flags: Right-sided displacement/torsion | tachycardia | shock
clinical_review_notes: RDA/abomasal volvulus can be a surgical emergency; do not present rolling as equivalent to definitive treatment.

signs: Severe vomiting | bloody diarrhea | fever | dehydration | lethargy | foul-smelling diarrhea
diagnosis: Parvovirus antigen/SNAP test | clinical signs | CBC/leukopenia
treatment_raw: Aggressive fluid/electrolyte support + antiemetic + nutrition + antibiotics when sepsis/neutropenia risk warrants; no routine specific antiviral
prevention: Core vaccination (DHPP/DA2PP) | isolation and disinfection
red_flags: Bloody diarrhea | repeated vomiting | severe dehydration | shock
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Fever | nasal/ocular discharge | cough | vomiting/diarrhea | twitching | seizures
diagnosis: Clinical suspicion | PCR/other laboratory testing as available | vaccination history
treatment_raw: Supportive care: fluids/nutrition, antibiotics only for secondary bacterial infection, anticonvulsants when required
prevention: Core vaccination
red_flags: Seizures | myoclonus | respiratory distress
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Bordetella bronchiseptica; parainfluenza and other respiratory pathogens
signs: Dry hacking cough | goose-honk cough | gagging | sneezing
treatment_raw: Rest/supportive care; doxycycline when bacterial Bordetella infection is suspected or clinically indicated; cough suppressant only in selected non-pneumonic cases
prevention: Bordetella and respiratory vaccination based on risk
red_flags: Fever | lethargy | productive cough | dyspnea suggesting pneumonia
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Flea allergy; food allergy; atopic dermatitis and other causes
signs: Itching | hair loss | erythema | paw licking | recurrent ear disease
diagnosis: Dermatologic exam | flea combing | cytology/skin scraping | diet trial/allergy workup as indicated
treatment_raw: Cause-specific therapy; flea control; anti-pruritic therapy may include oclacitinib or lokivetmab; corticosteroids only when appropriate; diet trial for food allergy
prevention: Consistent ectoparasite prevention | allergen management
red_flags: Facial swelling | breathing difficulty | severe skin infection
clinical_review_notes: Medication contraindications and patient-specific risks require veterinarian assessment.

cause: Bacterial/yeast infection often secondary to allergy, moisture or anatomy
signs: Head shaking | ear scratching | odor | erythema | discharge
treatment_raw: Ear cleaning when tympanum status permits + topical antimicrobial/antifungal/anti-inflammatory selected from cytology
prevention: Address underlying allergy | keep ears appropriately dry/clean
red_flags: Head tilt | neurologic signs | severe pain | ruptured tympanum concern
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Dietary indiscretion; toxin; many other causes
signs: Vomiting | anorexia | lethargy
diagnosis: Clinical exam; imaging/labs when foreign body, toxin, pancreatitis or systemic disease suspected
treatment_raw: Fluids as indicated + antiemetic such as maropitant when appropriate + gastroprotectant only when indicated; feeding plan individualized
prevention: Prevent garbage/toxin/foreign-body access
red_flags: Repeated vomiting | abdominal pain | distension | hematemesis | inability to keep water down
clinical_review_notes: Source note says NPO 12 h; prolonged fasting is not universally appropriate, especially in puppies or some disease states.

cause: Developmental hip joint laxity/osteoarthritis; genetic and environmental factors
signs: Hind-limb lameness | difficulty rising | bunny hopping | pain
diagnosis: Orthopedic examination | radiographs, often with sedation/positioning
treatment_raw: Weight management + exercise/rehabilitation + veterinarian-prescribed analgesia/NSAID + selected supplements; surgery for appropriate severe cases
prevention: Responsible breeding | weight control | appropriate growth management
red_flags: Non-weight-bearing lameness | severe acute pain
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Uterine infection in intact female dog
signs: Lethargy | increased drinking | vaginal discharge in open pyometra | anorexia | fever; often weeks after estrus
treatment_raw: Emergency ovariohysterectomy is standard definitive treatment in many cases + IV fluids + antibiotics; medical management only in selected specialist cases
prevention: Spaying
red_flags: Collapse | abdominal distension | sepsis | closed-cervix pyometra
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Vomiting | diarrhea | fever | severe dehydration | sudden death in kittens
diagnosis: FPV antigen/PCR as available | CBC/leukopenia | clinical signs
treatment_raw: Intensive supportive care: fluids/electrolytes, antiemetic, nutrition, antibiotics when bacterial translocation/sepsis risk warrants
prevention: Core FVRCP vaccination | isolation/disinfection
red_flags: Severe dehydration | hypothermia | collapse | very young kitten
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Feline herpesvirus-1; feline calicivirus; other pathogens
signs: Sneezing | nasal discharge | eye discharge | oral ulcers | fever
treatment_raw: Supportive care, hydration/nutrition, eye therapy when indicated; antibiotics only when secondary bacterial infection is suspected
prevention: FVRCP vaccination | reduce crowding/stress
red_flags: Open-mouth breathing | anorexia >24 h | corneal ulcer | severe dehydration
clinical_review_notes: Source notes mention lysine; routine lysine supplementation for FHV is not supported consistently and should not be ground truth.

cause: Idiopathic cystitis, uroliths, urethral plugs and other causes
signs: Straining to urinate | blood in urine | crying in litter box | genital licking | frequent small urinations
diagnosis: Urinalysis | imaging | clinical examination; rule out urethral obstruction
treatment_raw: Cause-specific treatment; analgesia and urinary diet/water strategies where appropriate; male urethral obstruction requires emergency catheterization/stabilization
prevention: Increase water intake | appropriate diet | stress/litter-box management
red_flags: Straining with little/no urine | vomiting | lethargy | painful bladder
clinical_review_notes: Routine antibiotics are not indicated for most young cats with FLUTD unless bacterial infection is documented.

signs: Increased drinking/urination | weight loss | vomiting | halitosis | poor appetite
diagnosis: Creatinine/BUN | SDMA where available | urinalysis/USG | blood pressure and staging
treatment_raw: Renal diet + hydration support + phosphate control/antiemetic/blood-pressure or proteinuria treatment based on stage and findings
prevention: Routine senior-cat screening; no guaranteed prevention
red_flags: Severe dehydration | anorexia | uremic signs | acute worsening
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Increased thirst/urination | increased appetite | weight loss
diagnosis: Persistent hyperglycemia + glucosuria; fructosamine when useful; rule out stress hyperglycemia
treatment_raw: Insulin therapy + appropriate diet + home/clinic glucose monitoring
prevention: Weight management may reduce risk
red_flags: Ketones | vomiting | lethargy | diabetic ketoacidosis signs
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Functional thyroid adenoma/adenomatous hyperplasia in older cats
signs: Weight loss despite appetite | hyperactivity | vomiting | increased thirst
diagnosis: Serum total T4; additional thyroid testing/imaging if equivocal
treatment_raw: Methimazole, radioactive iodine, surgery or iodine-restricted diet depending on case
prevention: No established routine prevention
red_flags: Severe tachycardia | heart failure signs | hypertension complications
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Coughing | wheezing | increased respiratory effort | open-mouth breathing
diagnosis: Thoracic radiographs + clinical assessment; rule out heartworm, infection and other causes
treatment_raw: Inhaled/systemic corticosteroid + bronchodilator when indicated; oxygen and emergency stabilization for severe attacks
prevention: Avoid smoke, aerosols and dusty litter where possible
red_flags: Open-mouth breathing | cyanosis | severe respiratory distress
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

signs: Itching | hair loss | flea dirt | visible ticks | anemia in severe flea burden
treatment_raw: Species-appropriate ectoparasiticide and environmental control; source notes list fipronil, afoxolaner/NexGard, fluralaner/Bravecto
prevention: Regular veterinarian-recommended flea/tick prevention
red_flags: Severe anemia in young animal | tick paralysis | systemic tick-borne disease signs
clinical_review_notes: Never generalize dog-only products to cats; permethrin-containing dog products can be highly toxic to cats.

signs: Diarrhea | weight loss | pot belly in young animals | vomiting worms | anemia with hookworms
treatment_raw: Parasite-specific deworming; source notes list fenbendazole, praziquantel and combination products
prevention: Age- and risk-based deworming/fecal testing + flea control for tapeworm prevention
red_flags: Severe anemia | melena | dehydration | failure to thrive
clinical_review_notes: Deworming every 3 months is not universally optimal; schedule should follow age, lifestyle and local parasite guidelines.

signs: Lameness | bleeding | fracture | pain | shock signs
diagnosis: Primary survey/physical exam | imaging and laboratory tests as indicated
treatment_raw: Hemorrhage control + stabilization/oxygen/IV access as indicated + veterinarian-prescribed analgesia + surgery/fracture management when required
prevention: Leash/carrier/fencing and safe environment
red_flags: Breathing difficulty | uncontrolled bleeding | pale gums | collapse | major fracture
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment

cause: Examples in notes: acetaminophen/paracetamol, chocolate, grapes/raisins, anticoagulant rodenticide
signs: Vomiting | diarrhea | tremors | seizures | pale gums | variable toxin-specific signs
treatment_raw: Immediate veterinary/poison-control guidance; decontamination only when appropriate; activated charcoal or antidotes such as vitamin K1 for anticoagulant rodenticide when indicated; IV/supportive therapy
prevention: Secure medications, foods, chemicals and rodenticides
red_flags: Seizures | breathing difficulty | collapse | known toxin ingestion | acetaminophen exposure in cats
clinical_review_notes: Do NOT encode 'induce vomiting if <2 h' as universal advice; emesis is contraindicated for many toxins/clinical states and must be directed by a veterinarian/poison service.

signs: Bad breath | drooling | difficulty eating | visible tartar | oral pain
diagnosis: Oral examination + dental probing/radiographs under anesthesia when indicated
treatment_raw: Professional dental cleaning under anesthesia + extraction of nonviable teeth when needed; antibiotics only for selected indications
prevention: Tooth brushing | veterinarian-approved dental products/chews | regular dental assessment
red_flags: Facial swelling | inability to eat | oral bleeding/mass
clinical_review_notes: Vet review required before clinical deployment
